title: Compression Vault
intro: Welcome to Basement Level One. The Compression Vault stores data reduction algorithms. Solve each puzzle to earn a digit of the exit code.

puzzles.title: Run-Length Encoding
puzzles.prompt:
Run-Length Encoding (RLE) compresses repeated characters. The string 'AAABBC' becomes '3A2B1C'.

How many characters long is the RLE encoding of 'AAAAABBBCCCCCD'?
(Count every character in the encoded result, including the numbers.)

variants.prompt:
Run-Length Encoding (RLE) compresses repeated characters. The string 'AAABBC' becomes '3A2B1C'.

How many UNIQUE letters appear in the RLE encoding of 'AAAAABBBCCCCCD'?
(Just count the distinct letter characters.)

hint.text: Break it down: 5 A's, 3 B's, 5 C's, 1 D. Write each as count+letter, then count all characters in the result.

puzzles.teachingPoint: RLE works best on data with long runs of identical values — like simple images with large solid-color areas. It's one of the simplest lossless compression algorithms.

puzzles.title: Best Compression Target
puzzles.prompt: Which of the following strings would compress BEST using Run-Length Encoding?

variants.prompt: Which of the following strings would compress WORST using Run-Length Encoding?

hint.text: RLE replaces consecutive repeated characters with a count + character. The longer the run, the better the compression.

puzzles.teachingPoint: RLE achieves its best compression ratio when the input has long consecutive runs of the same value. Random or alternating data actually EXPANDS under RLE — '1A1B1C' is longer than 'ABC'!

puzzles.title: Compression Ratio
puzzles.prompt:
A file is 900 bytes. After compression it's 300 bytes.

What is the compression ratio? (Enter as a whole number, e.g. if 2:1 enter 2)

variants.prompt:
A file is 1200 bytes. After compression it's 400 bytes.

What is the compression ratio? (Enter as a whole number, e.g. if 2:1 enter 2)

hint.text: Compression ratio = original size / compressed size.

puzzles.teachingPoint: Compression ratio tells you how much smaller the data got. A 3:1 ratio means the compressed file is one-third the original size. Typical ZIP compression achieves 2:1 to 10:1 depending on the data type.

puzzles.title: RLE Decode
puzzles.prompt:
Decode the following RLE string: '5A3B2C3D'

How many total characters are in the decoded output?

variants.prompt:
Decode the following RLE string: '4A2B3C4D'

How many total characters are in the decoded output?

hint.text: Add up all the numbers: they represent how many times each character repeats.

puzzles.teachingPoint: Decoding RLE is straightforward — just expand each count-character pair. This simplicity is what makes RLE fast for both encoding and decoding, ideal for real-time applications.

puzzles.title: Bandwidth Emergency
puzzles.prompt: Your network link can only transfer 100 MB/min. You need to send a 500 MB database backup in under 2 minutes. Which compression approach makes the most sense?
choices: Use a fast algorithm like LZ4 — it compresses less but runs in seconds, giving you time to transfer
Use maximum GZIP compression — smallest possible file, even though compression itself takes 3 minutes
Split into 5 files and send them sequentially without compression

variants.prompt: You're backing up a database nightly over a slow WAN link (50 MB/min). The backup is 2 GB. What's the most practical compression strategy?
choices: Use a balanced algorithm like ZSTD — good compression ratio with reasonable speed
Use no compression — it adds CPU overhead on the server
Use maximum bzip2 compression, even though it takes 30 minutes to compress
Compress with RLE only, since it's the fastest algorithm

hint.text: Think about total time: compression time + transfer time. Sometimes a faster (but less effective) algorithm wins because you save more on transfer than you spend on compression.

puzzles.teachingPoint: In real-world scenarios, compression is a time tradeoff. Fast algorithms (LZ4, Snappy, ZSTD) are often better than maximum compression when network transfer time dominates. Total time = compress time + transfer time.
